paraphrase: May we be capable (śakemahi) of the Nāciketa (fire), which is the bridge for those who sacrifice, and of that which is the imperishable, highest brahman, the fearless farther shore for those who wish to cross over. speaker: Yama (Death)
notes: Construal is uncertain: nāciketam can be read as the Nāciketa fire alone (the ritual bridge) with the brahman clause in apposition to it, or the two are set side by side; the commentators divide.
